newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Spain sets the stage for Endesa sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spain sets the stage for Endesa sale.

text.p: Spain on Thursday set the stage for its third and biggest privatisation this year, approving the sale of up to 35 percent of electricity giant Endesa.

In the wake of two hugely successful privatisations -- Telefonica De Espana and energy group Repsol SA -- the government laid out the preliminary details for its biggest sale yet of utility firm Endesa scheduled to begin towards the end of September.
Most analysts expect the privatisation to be a resounding success and said the details of the sale were largely in line with what had been expected.

"There are no surprises in the numbers," said Benito Vera, equity analyst at Salomon Brothers. "I think this is an attractive investment because the appetite for shares among the Spanish public is still high and I don't think there's going to be any problems for the operation."
The government still owns 66.8 percent of Endesa, via state holding company SEPI. It sold an initial five percent in 1950, and privatised a further 20 percent in 1988 and some nine percent in 1994.

Industry Minister Josep Pique said a stake of between 25 and 35 percent would be sold depending on market conditions at the time of the sale, raising between 750 billion ($4.8 billion) and one trillion pesetas ($6.5 billion) for state coffers.

"If sentiment remains as it is now, SEPI will go for 35 percent, but if the market turns pessimistic due to worries on Europe's monetary union for example, then it will sell less," Alberto Nunez, equity analyst at BBV said.
Analysts expect the government will sell a second and final tranche next year.
"The objective is that Endesa will be fully privatised by the end of 1998," a spokesman at SEPI said.

SEPI said 51.5 percent would directed to retail investors and six percent to employees. Of the remainder, 10 percent would be allocated for Spanish institutional investors and 32.5 percent to international investors.

"The fact that some 70 percent is going to domestic parties and just 30 percent internationally reflects the fact that international investors are not so keen to invest in the Spanish stock market with prices as they are," said Nunez.
Pique said retail investors would be offered a four percent discount, while employees will enjoy a 10 percent discount.
Pique also set out a preliminary calendar for the sale.

Spain's stock market commission CNMV and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is expected to authorise the prospectus around September 26 and the share offer will officially blast off on September 29.
The maximum price will be set on October 13 and the final price will be fixed around October 20, Pique said. The following day, the allotment will be approved with payment on October 24.
The government had initially planned to sell its remaining Endesa share in three lots, starting this year, analysts said.
But the unparallelled success of public share offerings in other blue chips such as Telefonica in February and energy group Repsol in April have encouraged the state to move faster.
The government sold its remaining 10 percent share in Repsol in April and its final 20.9 percent stake in Telefonica in February.
